label: Well-Adjusted Graduate Male
summary: This profile represents respondents who report notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. They demonstrate strong psychological well-being across all three measured dimensions, with anxiety scores near floor level and depression and loneliness scores well below typical thresholds of concern.
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate-level education or above, 1–3 hours of daily screen/internet use
behavior_markers: Very low loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 0.79), suggesting robust social connectedness
Minimal depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.28), well below clinical concern thresholds
Near-zero anxiety symptoms (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.04), indicating very low generalized anxiety
Moderate and controlled screen/internet use (1–3 hours daily)
Higher educational attainment, which may serve as a protective factor for mental health

label: Lonely, Distressed High-Screen-Time Graduate Women
summary: This profile captures highly educated women who spend more than five hours daily on screens and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Their UCLA-8 loneliness scores (mean 1.72), PHQ-9 depression scores (mean 1.73), and GAD-7 anxiety scores (mean 2.14) are all in the higher range, suggesting a co-occurring pattern of psychological distress. The cluster is sizable (n = 181), indicating this is not a fringe pattern but a meaningful subgroup within the sample.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, more than 5 hours of daily screen time
behavior_markers: Elevated loneliness (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.72), indicating persistent feelings of social disconnection
Higher depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 1.73), suggesting frequent low mood, fatigue, or loss of interest
Notably high anxiety levels (GAD-7 mean ≈ 2.14), the most pronounced distress indicator in this profile
Extended daily screen time exceeding 5 hours, potentially reflecting both occupational demands and coping or avoidance behaviors
Co-occurrence of all three distress dimensions, pointing to a compounding mental health burden
tone: Concerned and empathetic; this profile reflects a population segment experiencing significant, multi-dimensional psychological distress that warrants attention in both research and intervention design.

label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
